hints.title: Forward Scan Discount Obstacle
hints.text: Scanning forward for the next smaller or equal price for every item takes quadratic time. How can keeping unresolved item indices in an ordered sequence apply discounts immediately when a qualifying price appears?

hints.title: Monotonic Increasing Index Invariant
hints.text: Indices in the sequence have strictly increasing price values. When an item with price prices[i] appears, it provides the discount for all earlier indices whose prices are >= prices[i].

hints.title: In-Place Discount Procedure
hints.text: Copy prices into a result array. Maintain an index list. For each index i and price prices[i]: while the list is non-empty and prices[list[-1]] >= prices[i], pop index j and subtract prices[i] from res[j]. Append i to the list. Return res.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Each index is pushed and popped at most once to apply immediate discounts.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Scanning subsequent items for each item takes O(N^2) comparisons.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: An auxiliary index list enables immediate discount resolution in strictly linear O(N) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizing next smaller or equal element problem and applying discount updates cleanly.
